endorsements.quote: Therefore, PDTs must include mechanisms for accountability and recourse that clarify how decisions are documented; how disagreements are handled; and what happens when model-guided recommendations are questioned, overridden, or followed with adverse consequences.

Therefore, PDTs should incorporate translation mechanisms, potentially including GenAI-mediated dialogue, that allow users to ask questions, request clarification, and explore alternatives in plain language.

Evaluation should instead examine whether users can meaningfully understand and work with model-driven information, whether the system supports participatory quality during use, and whether these benefits are sustained over time.

Through feedback loops that connect these layers, patient input can inform interpretation and guide ongoing system refinement, helping ensure that digital twins remain aligned with patients’ changing realities over time.

unlisted_practices: Present multiple plausible scenarios and explain trade-offs rather than issuing a single directive recommendation.
Make model uncertainty visible to users through intuitive visualizations and explanations.

Constrain generative AI to grounded tasks such as explaining traceable model outputs, eliciting missing context, comparing predefined scenarios, and signaling uncertainty, not inventing clinical rationales or ungrounded advice.
Pair generative AI interaction layers with safeguards such as source attribution, audit trails, uncertainty signaling, and clinician review in higher-risk situations.
Allow users to annotate and correct missing, outdated, or misinterpreted context in model inputs.
Explicitly attribute proxy or caregiver input rather than treating it as interchangeable with first-person patient input.
Provide nondigital alternatives and accommodations for patients with low digital literacy, limited language concordance, or unreliable digital access.
Make data provenance transparent so patients can verify what information drives the model.
Support selective disclosure and make explicit who contributed, can view, can modify, and can act on sensitive contextual information.
Frame recommendations as options for negotiation rather than prescriptive orders, keeping participatory interaction complementary to clinical judgment.
Evaluate patient comprehension, engagement, and shared decision-making quality, using vignette-based studies, pilots, and short longitudinal deployments, rather than only predictive accuracy.
